summary: The reference Arduino since 2010: an ATmega328P at 16 MHz with 32 KB of flash, a USB-serial chip of its own and the header layout every shield follows.

revisions.name: R1
revisions.changes: ATmega8U2 as the USB-to-serial converter in place of the FTDI chip of earlier boards.

revisions.name: R2
revisions.changes: Added a resistor pulling the ATmega8U2's HWB line to ground, making it easier to put the USB chip into DFU mode.

revisions.name: R3
revisions.changes: The 1.0 pinout: SDA and SCL pins beside AREF, IOREF and a spare pin beside RESET; a stronger reset circuit; the ATmega16U2 replaces the 8U2.

pinout.note: R3 layout; R1 and R2 lack IOREF and the SDA/SCL pins by AREF

gotchas.title: 2 KB of RAM goes fast
gotchas.text: String literals are copied into RAM unless they are kept in flash with PROGMEM or wrapped in F(); text-heavy sketches fill the 2 KB of SRAM long before the flash.

gotchas.title: Pins 0 and 1 are the USB serial
gotchas.text: D0 and D1 carry the serial link to the computer; anything connected to them can interfere with Serial output and cause failed uploads.

gotchas.title: 5 V logic
gotchas.text: I/O is 5 V. Sensors and modules that run at 3.3 V (most modern ones) need level shifting on their inputs.

rows.label: USB

editorial.today: Still the board most tutorials, shields and classrooms assume. For new designs that need more memory or Wi-Fi, the Uno R4 keeps the layout.

revisions.changes: 256 MB of RAM. The I2C pins on P1 are GPIO0 and GPIO1, and pin 13 is GPIO21.

revisions.changes: I2C moved to GPIO2 and GPIO3, pin 13 became GPIO27, and mounting holes were added. Still 256 MB at first.

gotchas.text: Three header pins changed between revisions: pin 3 and 5 are GPIO0/GPIO1 on revision 1 but GPIO2/GPIO3 on revision 2, and pin 13 is GPIO21 on revision 1 but GPIO27 on revision 2. Old tutorials often assume one or the other.

gotchas.title: ARMv6 only
gotchas.text: The BCM2835 is ARMv6. Many Linux distributions only ship ARMv7 or 64-bit Arm builds, so use 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS.

editorial.history: Raspberry Pi was created by a UK charity to get children programming again. The Model B went on sale on 29 February 2012; demand crashed the distributors' websites, and it shipped with 256 MB of RAM until the 512 MB version replaced it at the same price in October 2012.
editorial.today: Slow by modern standards and limited to 32-bit software, but fine for a headless sensor logger, a retro emulator for 8-bit systems, or learning GPIO basics with Python. Pick a Zero 2 W or Pi 4 for anything that needs a desktop or modern web browser.

gotchas.text: GPIO is 3.3 V and the RP2040's absolute maximum on an I/O pin is IOVDD + 0.5 V, so 5 V logic can damage it; use a level shifter.

gotchas.text: The RP2040 ADC's differential non-linearity peaks at four codes (512, 1536, 2560 and 3584), erratum RP2040-E11, which is not fixed, and its reference comes from the noisy 3.3 V supply. For better accuracy, fit an external reference on ADC_VREF or use an external ADC.

gotchas.title: GP25 is the LED
gotchas.text: On the Pico the on-board LED is GPIO25. The Pico W drives its LED from the wireless chip instead, so LED code is not interchangeable between them.

power.note: An on-board buck-boost converter makes 3.3 V from VSYS, so a single Li-ion cell or three AA cells in series can power it directly.
